svg.title: Proposition 23: adaptive physical-descriptor selection under a shared base confidence ball
svg.desc: What this figure shows: This proposition extends the P22 simultaneous finite-sample construction from a fixed refinement chain to data-dependent selection among candidate physical refinements. Its purpose is to control a common scientific workflow: inspect finite data, compare several physically motivated refinements, and choose the refinement that appears to remove the largest.. Visible guideposts include: One base confidence ball remains valid after selecting a deterministic physical refinement from the same data.; SHARED BASE EVENT; Control the finite physical-target law before selection; ‖PΩE − P̂ΩE‖TV ≤ τn(α); Pr(event) ≥ 1 − α; The probability statement is made once at the base-law level.. How to read it: follow the diagram in the direction of its arrows and use each box, panel, inequality, or highlighted region only with the meaning printed beside it. Main takeaway: this is the visual companion to Proposition 23; the proposition document supplies the assumptions, proof, and exact scope of every implication. Scientific status: Proposition 23 theorem/certificate visual. It is not independent empirical evidence and does not, by itself, identify a physical or latent variable with consciousness.
svg.text: P23 · Adaptive Physical-Descriptor Selection Certification
One base confidence ball remains valid after selecting a deterministic physical refinement from the same data.
SHARED BASE EVENT
Control the finite physical-target law before selection
‖PΩE − P̂ΩE‖TV ≤ τn(α)
Pr(event) ≥ 1 − α
The probability statement is made once at the base-law level.
UNIFORM PUSHFORWARD CONTROL
Every deterministic descriptor inherits the event
∀f: ‖f#P − f#P̂‖TV ≤ ‖P − P̂‖TV
Residual and gain laws are deterministic pushforwards of (Ω,E).
No candidate-wise probability union bound is introduced.
DATA-DEPENDENT SELECTION
Choose the empirically strongest admissible refinement
f̂ ∈ arg maxf Ĝf
The selected gain and residual retain their simultaneous intervals.
Selection can use the same fixed-n sample because coverage is pathwise.
POST-SELECTION NEAR-OPTIMALITY
The selected refinement is certified relative to the best admissible candidate
0 ≤ G* − Gf̂ ≤ maxf UfG − Lf̂G ≤ 2Γmax
Rf̂ − minf Rf = G* − Gf̂
The same regret bound controls excess residual because P21 gives Rf = Rc − Gf.
NOT OPTIONAL STOPPING
P23 is fixed-n. Repeated looks across growing sample sizes need an anytime-valid theorem.
PHYSICAL INTERPRETATION
Statistical post-selection validity does not make a target-engineered map a physical explanation.
P23 certifies adaptive choice within the declared physical model; it does not establish physical completeness or nonphysical ontology.
